text:
jess: Sketching a mixed-capacity topology: 'reserve buffer + transient lanes' — min on-demand buffer per region, ephemeral preemptible GPU lanes for burst. Looking for ops/runtime tradeoffs. :thinking:

kai: Nice. Quick Q: how small can the reserve be before it breaks tail latency? We need to consider scale-up time for on-demand GPUs (4-6 mins).

priya: Proposal: set region_min_reserve = max(1 node, 10% of steady q95 traffic). Label nodes: node.k8s.io/capacity=reserve vs capacity=ephemeral. Use PodPriority + tolerations for preemptible lane pods.

jess: Agree. Also want soft handoff: when ephemeral evicted, traffic routes to reserve, not drop. Requires graceful connection draining + model KV checkpointing (avoid cold restarts).

infra-bot: autoscaler-recommender: try configuring CA with `--expander=least-waste` + `--scale-down-delay=10m` for GPU nodegroups. Recommended min nodes per AZ = 1 for reserve.

kai: Checkpointing KV caches is hard. For big contexts, restoring cache on a new GPU costs ~100-300ms per token at first. Options: (a) warm standby with warmed KV on a tiny set of nodes, (b) short-lived prefix caching + accept latency tail.

priya: Operational pattern: preStop hook to flush hot prefixes to redis/S3 and background rebuild on new node. Example: `preStop: exec: ["/bin/sh","-c","curl -sS http://localhost:8080/kv/flush || true"]`. Also use PDBs to limit concurrent evacuations.

jess: I like the eviction credits model — give tenants X ephemeral-minutes/month (burst tokens). When bucket empty, route to reserve or downgrade model. Keeps cost accountability and protects reserve from noisy tenants.

sam: Network caveat: cross-AZ fallback will increase inter-AZ egress and add latency for KV syncs. For KV-heavy workloads prefer same-AZ fallback or session transfer via redis with sticky routing.

kai: Cost tradeoff: reserve floor too high kills spot savings. Suggest dynamic floor: floor(t) = p90(usage, 1h) * safety_factor. Tune safety_factor against SLA (start at 1.2).

priya: Also weight ephemeral allocation by interruption probability per instance type. Newer GPU SKUs typically have lower preempt rates — favor those for critical burst lanes.

jess: Routing policy sketch: 1) route to ephemeral same-AZ, 2) ephemeral cross-AZ within region, 3) reserve on-demand same-AZ, 4) fallback to smaller model. Need metrics per step to measure impact.

priya: Key metrics to emit: eviction_rate, fallback_rate, kv_restore_latency, warmup_time, cost_per_token, tail_latency_q99. Alert if fallback_rate > 0.5% or eviction_rate > 1%.

kai: Implementation notes: use nodeAffinity + taints. Example node selector: `nodeSelector: {"node.k8s.io/capacity":"ephemeral"}` and `tolerations` for preemptible. Autoscaler should watch a custom metric `tokens_per_gpu`.

jess: Test plan: A/B run in staging-east1 for 2 weeks with 10% production traffic. Inject spot drains and measure tail latency, restore time, and cost delta. I'll own the runbook and rollout steps.

sam: I'll own network/redis sticky-transfer flow. priya own autoscaler tuning. kai will prototype KV warm pool. @all :thumbsup:

jess: Next actions: priya create CA config PR, kai prototype warm pool, sam update network runbook. We'll reconvene after initial staging test.
